title: Nanobeam Ultrafast Electron Diffraction of Structural Phase Transformations in Charge-Density Wave Materials
content: Optical control over charge-ordered phases promises the tuning of macroscopic properties of quantum materials and the realization of metastable states. Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), for example, are characterized by strong electron-phonon coupling that favors the occurrence of exciting physical phenomena, including the formation of charge-density waves (CDWs) [1]. This additional periodic modulation of the crystal charge density leads to the opening of an electronic band gap, resulting in a change of the material’s electrical conductivity. Pulsed laser excitation has been shown to efficiently suppress CDW order or induce transitions between different phases. The structural counterpart of CDW formation, a periodic lattice distortion (PLD), is accessible by scattering probes. In particular, ultrafast electron diffraction (UED) and microscopy elucidate the femtosecond evolution of lattice symmetries and phonon populations after an optical quench [2].
